passage:
The computer lab closed at nine, Tarun's data pack had almost run out, and the problem set was due at midnight. Tarun worked through question after question by hand, erasing and trying again, hunched over one desk in a noisy corridor.

Across the room, Anand finished the whole set in ten minutes with an AI tool, closed the laptop and left for tea. Next week the marks came back: Anand scored higher. Tarun felt foolish, as if hours of effort had bought nothing.

A month later, at a mock interview, the panel asked Anand to explain one solution on the whiteboard. Anand's marker stayed still.

Tarun, on the other hand, had used the AI as a tutor that night, asking it to explain the one step that didn't click, and could walk through every line.

qa.q: What time did the computer lab close?
qa.a: The computer lab closed at nine.

qa.q: How did Tarun feel when the marks came back, and why?
qa.a: Tarun felt foolish, as if hours of effort had bought nothing, because Anand scored higher after finishing in ten minutes.

qa.q: What did Tarun do with the AI that helped later?
qa.a: Tarun used it as a tutor to explain the one step that didn't click, so Tarun could walk through every line, while Anand copied without understanding.

qa.q: How might Anand feel at the mock interview?
qa.a: Anand probably felt exposed and stuck, with the marker staying still, because the shortcut left no understanding to explain.

grounding: Tarun envies Anand's quick, high-scoring AI work and feels foolish, but shortcuts show at the interview while using AI as a tutor builds real skill.
